evidence: Ter. Eun. 3.1.61: Bene dīxtī, “you are right” (Lewis & Short s.v. bene: “a formula of approbation”)

terms.comment: Traupman’s phrase; Terence’s rēctē putās is the attested one.

evidence: Plaut. Capt. 1.2.73; Ter. Eun. 2.2.57, 3.1.37 (Lewis & Short s.v. facētus)
terms.comment: Praise for a witty remark rather than a true one: facētē, wittily.

terms.gloss: you’re right, what you say is true
evidence: Plaut. Am. 1.1.239: vēra dīcō (Lewis & Short s.v. vērus)
Plaut. Cas. 2.3.18: vēra dīcās velim, I wish you told the truth (Lewis & Short s.v. volō)
terms.comment: Plautus’ vēra dīcere, to tell the truth; the second person is Traupman’s, built the same way.

phrases.english: “He didn’t bring it! The Minotaur stays at Conimbriga!” “You’re right.”
phrases.source: Libellus III, Apud avum et aviam

phrases.english: You’re right (what you say is true).
